titulo: Everything with tongs: each agent's model and the tool that comes in (or not)
lead: Every week a new repository shows up promising everything. Handle it with tongs: before installing, ask your AI whether it fits your stack and what you gain. And don't use the same model for everything: each agent can have its own, among the best, the economical and the free.
objetivo: choose each agent's model by cost and task, and test any new tool against your stack before installing it.

aprende.t: Three model tiers: the best, the economical and the free
Four questions before you install any tool
Two opinions on a sensitive topic
Why the plan takes longer than the execution

hero_alt: Precision tweezers on a light workbench, next to a small circuit board.

nos.detalhe: A coworker, a video, a post: "you have to use this." It's not a decision yet, it's a candidate.
Ask the AI that already knows your context. A tool in a different language, or one that repeats what you already have, usually stays out, no matter how good it is.
Passed all four? Test it on a single task, with a deadline, before rolling it out.
Write down why it stayed out. The next time someone recommends it, the answer is already written.

secoes.sub: Three tiers. The names change every month; the criteria stay.

texto: Coding, finance and decisions involving money call for the strongest model your plan offers.
The cost of an error here is higher than the price difference.
Customer service, triage and summaries run many times a day. A cheaper, faster model can handle them.
Test with 20 real cases before switching.
There are open, free models with huge context windows, good for prototyping and for tasks with no sensitive data.
Check the provider's data policy: free sometimes means your data trains the model.
For a financial plan, ask two agents running different models for the same analysis, with the same context, and compare.
Where they agree, you gain confidence; where they disagree, that's the question you need to ask.

secoes.sub: Run the first one in the AI that already knows your project.

blocos.conteudo:
Someone recommended this tool to me: <name and link>.
You know my stack (languages, services, what's already running).

Answer in up to 10 lines:
1. DOES IT FIT? What language and infrastructure does it run on, and does that work with my stack?
2. DO I ALREADY HAVE IT? What I already use that does the same thing or close to it.
3. WHAT DO I GAIN? One concrete task that would get better, with a number if possible.
4. RISK? Data access, maintenance, license, dependence on third parties.

Verdict: IN (<deadline> test on one task) or OUT (reason in 1 line).

DATE       | TOOL            | VERDICT   | REASON
<dd/mm>    | <name>          | out       | different language, repeats what the CRM already does
<dd/mm>    | <name>          | in        | 2-week test on the purchasing agent

secoes.sub: Use a real recommendation you received.

exercicios.texto: Take the last tool or repository someone recommended to you and run the prompt in the AI that knows your project.
exercicios.pronto: you have the 4 answers and a verdict, IN or LEFT OUT, noted in the log.

exercicios.texto: Go back to the orchestra map (lesson 3) and mark each agent's tier: best, economical or free.
exercicios.pronto: every agent on the map has a tier and the reason in a few words.

secoes.sub: The lesson's mechanism explained in about two and a half minutes.

perguntas.p: A colleague recommends an excellent repository, but it's all in another language and repeats what your system already does. What do you do?
opcoes: Install it: if it's excellent, it's worth it
Rewrite your system in its language
Leave it out and note the reason in the log
perguntas.explica: A good tool that doesn't fit your stack and repeats what you already have brings upkeep with no gain. The log saves you from redoing the analysis when someone recommends it again.

perguntas.p: Which agent deserves the strongest model?
opcoes: The one that summarizes the day's meetings
The one that touches the group's financial plan
The one that answers frequently asked questions
perguntas.explica: Where a mistake is costly (money, code in use, a decision), pay for the best. Summaries and frequently asked questions run a lot and are fine with an economical model.

perguntas.p: Two agents with the same context disagreed about the cash plan. Is that bad?
opcoes: No: the disagreement shows you the question to investigate
Yes: one of the two agents is broken and needs to leave the team
Yes: it only makes sense to use one model per company
perguntas.explica: The second opinion is there to reveal weak points. Where they agree, you can trust it more; where they disagree, you need more analysis, yours and not theirs.

perguntas.p: A free model has a huge context. What should you watch out for before using it?
opcoes: Nothing: free with a large context is always the best choice
Use it only for finance tasks
Read the data policy and avoid sensitive data
perguntas.explica: Free can mean the provider uses your data. Great for a prototype and for tasks with no sensitive data; not for a client's accounting.

itens.texto: Four questions before installing: fit, already have, gain, risk.
Best where mistakes cost a lot, economical for volume, free for prototypes.
On a sensitive topic, compare two models with the same context.
What was left out is noted with the reason.
